questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.learningObjective: identify the purpose of semantic HTML elements
questions.stem: Which HTML element is most appropriate for the main navigation links of a page?

options.misconception: uses a generic container where a semantic element exists
uses an inline element for a block-level structure
confuses a content section with navigation

questions.explanation: The nav element is specifically designed for major navigation blocks, which improves accessibility and semantics. A div is generic and carries no meaning, a span is inline and unsuited to a navigation block, and a section groups thematic content rather than links, so each distractor names a real element applied to the wrong purpose.
questions.hint: Which element has navigation as its purpose?

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.learningObjective: identify the role of the doctype declaration
questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration at the start of a document?

options.text: It tells the browser to render the page in standards mode
It imports the HTML5 JavaScript library
options.misconception: confuses a declaration with a script import

options.text: It defines the document's root element
options.misconception: confuses doctype with the html element

options.text: It sets the default character encoding
options.misconception: confuses doctype with the meta charset tag

questions.explanation: The doctype declaration switches the browser to standards mode so layout and CSS behave per the HTML specification. It does not import libraries, define the root element, or set encoding, which are handled by script, html, and meta tags respectively.
questions.hint: Think about how browsers decide rendering mode.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.stem: Which of these elements is inline by default, so it does not force a new line?

options.misconception: treats a block container as inline
treats a paragraph block as inline
treats a sectioning block as inline

questions.explanation: Span is an inline element that flows within text without breaking lines. Div, p, and section are block-level elements that occupy their own line and stack vertically by default.
questions.hint: Which one sits inside a sentence?

questions.learningObjective: identify appropriate input types for data
questions.stem: Which input type should be used so a browser shows a date picker for a birthdate field?

options.misconception: uses free text where a native picker exists
adds unnecessary time selection for a date-only value
uses numeric input without date validation or picker

questions.explanation: The date input type renders a native date picker and validates a date value. Text requires manual formatting, datetime-local adds a time component not needed, and number lacks date semantics and picker UI.
questions.hint: Which type name matches the data being collected?

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.stem: How should a label be programmatically associated with an input for accessibility?

options.text: Match the label's for attribute to the input's id
Match the label's name attribute to the input's id
options.misconception: confuses name with the linking attribute

options.text: Wrap the input in a div with the same class
options.misconception: uses styling hooks instead of semantic association

options.text: Place the label after the input without attributes
options.misconception: relies on visual proximity rather than programmatic link

questions.explanation: Associating for with id creates an accessible name and lets clicking the label focus the control. Name is for form submission, class is for styling, and visual order alone does not establish the programmatic relationship.
questions.hint: Which attributes create the accessible link?

questions.stem: Among these selectors, which has the highest specificity?

options.misconception: uses class selectors instead of an id
uses a type plus class, lower than an id
chains classes but still lacks an id

questions.explanation: The selector with an id plus two classes and an element outranks selectors that use only classes and elements. An id contributes the highest single weight, so any selector containing one beats those without.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.stem: An element has width 200px, padding 10px on each side, border 5px on each side, and margin 15px on each side. What is its total horizontal space in pixels under the standard box model?
questions.explanation: Total horizontal space equals width plus left and right padding, border, and margin: 200 + 20 + 10 + 30 = 260. Padding contributes 20, border 10, and margin 30 on top of the 200px width.
questions.hint: Add width, padding, border, and margin on both sides.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.stem: In a flex container with flex-direction: row, which property distributes space between items along the horizontal axis?

options.misconception: confuses cross-axis alignment with main-axis distribution
confuses wrapping behavior with spacing
confuses multi-line cross-axis alignment with main-axis spacing

questions.explanation: justify-content controls distribution along the main axis, which is horizontal when flex-direction is row. align-items and align-content affect the cross axis, and flex-wrap only controls whether items wrap to new lines.

questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) defines three columns each taking one fraction of available space. The other options use invalid or wrong-property syntax that will not produce the intended column layout.

questions.stem: Which meta tag ensures a page scales correctly on mobile devices?

confuses SEO description with layout scaling
confuses auto-refresh with responsive scaling

questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag sets the layout width to the device width and initial zoom level, enabling responsive design. The other meta tags handle encoding, SEO, or refresh and do not affect scaling.

uses range syntax incorrectly for this context
matches exactly 600px rather than a range

questions.explanation: max-width: 600px matches viewports 600px or narrower. min-width matches 600px and wider, exact width matches only 600px, and the range syntax shown is not the standard form taught here.

questions.learningObjective: distinguish let, const, and var scoping
questions.stem: Which declaration creates a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?

options.misconception: block-scoped but reassignable
function-scoped and reassignable
not a standard variable declaration keyword

questions.explanation: const declares a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned. let is block-scoped but reassignable, var is function-scoped, and static is not used for local variables in this way.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.stem: What does the === operator do in JavaScript?

options.text: Compares value and type without coercion
Compares value only with type coercion
options.misconception: describes == instead of ===

options.text: Assigns a value and returns it
options.misconception: confuses equality with assignment
describes object identity rather than strict equality

questions.explanation: Strict equality (===) compares both value and type without implicit conversion. == coerces types, = assigns, and reference checks are a narrower concept than strict equality.
questions.hint: How many equals signs and what does strict mean?

selects by class, not id
selects by tag name, not id

text.explanation: getElementById is the dedicated, efficient method for retrieving an element by its id. querySelector can also do it with a # selector but is more general, while the other methods select by class or tag.

text.stem: Which property sets the plain text content of an element without parsing HTML?

considers CSS visibility and triggers reflow

text.explanation: textContent sets or gets raw text without HTML parsing. innerHTML and outerHTML parse markup, and innerText is CSS-aware and can trigger layout, so textContent is the safest plain-text choice.

text.stem: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?

confuses null with a falsy primitive type

text.explanation: Due to a historical bug, typeof null returns "object". It does not return "null", "undefined", or "boolean", so code should check null explicitly with === null.
